title: Ancient Greek Literature (c. 800–146 BCE) - Classical
body: Foundation of Western literature through epic poetry (Homer's Iliad, Odyssey), lyric poetry (Sappho), drama (Aeschylus, Sophocles).

title: Homer (c. 8th Century BCE) - Classical
body: Works: The Iliad, The Odyssey | Father of Western epic poetry; established narrative structures still used today.

title: Sappho (c. 630–570 BCE) - Classical
body: Works: Lyric poetry fragments | Premier lyric poet of antiquity; voice of personal emotion and love.

title: Aeschylus (c. 525–456 BCE) - Classical
body: Works: The Oresteia, Prometheus Bound | Father of Tragedy; introduced the second actor to drama.

title: Sophocles (c. 497–406 BCE) - Classical
body: Works: Oedipus Rex, Antigone | Perfection of Greek tragedy; exploration of fate vs. free will.

title: Ancient Roman Literature (c. 300 BCE – 400 CE) - Classical
body: Adapted Greek forms while emphasizing state duty, satire, rhetoric, and historical narratives.

title: Quintus Ennius (239–169 BCE) - Classical
body: Works: Annales (national epic), tragedies | 'Father of Roman poetry'; introduced dactylic hexameter to Latin.

title: Virgil (70–19 BCE) - Classical
body: Works: The Aeneid, Eclogues | Rome's national poet; bridged Greek tradition with Roman identity.

title: Horace (65–8 BCE) - Classical
body: Works: Odes, Satires, Epistles, Ars Poetica | Master of lyric poetry and literary criticism; perfected Latin meter and wit.

title: Ovid (43 BCE – 17 CE) - Classical
body: Works: Metamorphoses | Master of mythology and narrative transformation; huge influence on Renaissance art.

title: Medieval Literature (c. 500–1400 CE) - Medieval
body: Religious devotion, chivalric romance, allegory, and emerging vernacular languages dominated literary expression.

title: Dante Alighieri (1265–1321) - Medieval
body: Works: The Divine Comedy | Father of Italian literature; synthesized medieval theology and politics; one of the greatest poets in world literature.

title: Geoffrey Chaucer (c. 1343–1400) - Medieval
body: Works: The Canterbury Tales | Father of English literature; legitimized Middle English as a literary language.

title: The Renaissance (c. 1400–1600) - Renaissance
body: Rebirth of classical learning, humanism, individualism, and artistic flourishing across Europe.

title: Francesco Petrarch (1304–1374) - Renaissance
body: Works: Canzoniere | Father of Humanism; perfected the Sonnet form.

title: Michel de Montaigne (1533–1592) - Renaissance
body: Works: Essays | Inventor of the personal essay; explored human skepticism.

title: William Shakespeare (1564–1616) - Renaissance
body: Works: Hamlet, King Lear, Sonnet 18 | Greatest playwright in the English language; master of human psychology.

title: Miguel de Cervantes (1547–1616) - Renaissance
body: Works: Don Quixote | Author of the first modern novel; satire of chivalric romance.

title: John Milton (1608–1674) - Renaissance
body: Works: Paradise Lost | Epic poet of the Puritan age; explored themes of free will and rebellion.

title: Neoclassical / Enlightenment (c. 1660–1790) - Enlightenment
body: Reason, order, logic, and satire characterized this age of intellectual and social commentary.

title: Molière (1622–1673) - Enlightenment
body: Works: Tartuffe, The Miser | Master of French comedy; criticized hypocrisy and social pretense.

title: Jonathan Swift (1667–1745) - Enlightenment
body: Works: Gulliver's Travels | Master of satire; critiqued human nature and politics.

title: Voltaire (1694–1778) - Enlightenment
body: Works: Candide | Leading figure of the Enlightenment; advocated for civil liberties and reason.

title: David Hume (1711–1776) - Enlightenment
body: Works: A Treatise of Human Nature, Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion | Key figure of the Scottish Enlightenment; empiricist philosopher.

title: Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) - Enlightenment
body: Works: Critique of Pure Reason, Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals | Central figure of modern philosophy; synthesized rationalism and empiricism.

title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) - Enlightenment
body: Works: Faust, The Sorrows of Young Werther | Giant of German literature; bridged Enlightenment and Romanticism.

title: Romanticism (c. 1790–1850) - Romantic
body: Emotion, nature, imagination, and individualism rebelled against industrialization and rational constraints.

title: Jane Austen (1775–1817) - Romantic
body: Works: Pride and Prejudice, Emma | Master of social commentary and the novel of manners.

title: William Wordsworth (1770–1850) - Romantic
body: Works: Lyrical Ballads | Launching figure of Romanticism; focused on nature and common language.

title: Victor Hugo (1802–1885) - Romantic
body: Works: Les Misérables, The Hunchback of Notre-Dame | Leader of French Romanticism; champion of social justice.

title: Realism & Naturalism (c. 1850–1900) - Realism
body: Depicted everyday life and social issues through objective observation and deterministic perspectives.

title: Charles Dickens (1812–1870) - Realism
body: Works: Great Expectations, A Christmas Carol | Critic of Victorian industrial society; master of character and plot.

title: Leo Tolstoy (1828–1910) - Realism
body: Works: War and Peace, Anna Karenina | Peak of Realism; explored history, morality, and psychology.

title: Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821–1881) - Realism
body: Works: Crime and Punishment, The Brothers Karamazov | Psychological depth; explored faith, doubt, and existentialism.

title: Mark Twain (1835–1910) - Realism
body: Works: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn | Father of American literature; used vernacular speech and satire.

title: Henrik Ibsen (1828–1906) - Realism
body: Works: A Doll's House | Father of modern realism in drama; challenged social norms.

title: Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900) - Realism
body: Works: Thus Spoke Zarathustra, Beyond Good and Evil | Influential philosopher; critique of traditional morality and religion; concept of the Übermensch.

title: Modernism (c. 1900–1945) - Modernism
body: Fragmentation, experimentation, and stream of consciousness reflected disillusionment with traditional values.

title: Joseph Conrad (1857–1924) - Modernism
body: Works: Heart of Darkness | Explored imperialism and the human psyche; bridge to Modernism.

title: James Joyce (1882–1941) - Modernism
body: Works: Ulysses, Dubliners | Master of stream of consciousness; revolutionized the novel form.

title: T.S. Eliot (1888–1965) - Modernism
body: Works: The Waste Land | Defining poet of Modernism; captured post-WWI disillusionment.

title: Ernest Hemingway (1899–1961) - Modernism
body: Works: The Old Man and the Sea, A Farewell to Arms | Iceberg Theory of writing; voice of the Lost Generation.

title: George Orwell (1903–1950) - Modernism
body: Works: 1984, Animal Farm | Political satire; warned against totalitarianism.

title: Postmodernism (c. 1945–1990) - Postmodern
body: Irony, metafiction, and pastiche questioned grand narratives and embraced ambiguity and playfulness.

title: Vladimir Nabokov (1899–1977) - Postmodern
body: Works: Lolita | Master of prose style; played with narrative reliability.

title: Toni Morrison (1931–2019) - Postmodern
body: Works: Beloved, Song of Solomon | Explored African American experience; Nobel Prize winner.

title: Contemporary Literature (1990–Present) - Contemporary
body: Globalization, digital culture, identity politics, and diverse voices shape current literary landscape.
